transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. I guess... I'm here because I've been having these nights where I just... I eat an amount of food that kind of scares me. Like, I'll start with just some leftovers after I finish grading papers, and then... I don't know, I just end up going through cereal, crackers, peanut butter... even the snacks I pack for my classroom. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during these episodes?

Um... no. Not really. 

It's... once I start, it just feels like... I don't know. Like the reasonable teacher part of me is just watching from the outside. Just telling myself, 'Joan, stop.' But... my hands just keep opening things. I just keep putting food in my mouth until I'm... painfully full. So, no.
How do you feel after one of these eating episodes?

Um... guilty, I guess. Really bad. So I try to... fix it. 

The next day, I'll just tell myself I'm not allowed to eat breakfast or lunch at school. And... I'll usually stay out on the running trail for hours after work, or... or do extra yoga. Even if I'm feeling really shaky and exhausted, I just... I feel like I have to.
How often do these episodes of eating a large amount of food happen?

Um... I guess for the past few months... there's rarely a week without at least one night where I do that. Where I eat way more than I meant to. And then... yeah, the next day I just try to make up for it... by not eating at school, or pushing myself on a long walk or extra yoga.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after one of these eating episodes?
No. Um... no, I don't do that.
Do you ever use laxatives or diuretics to try to counteract the effects of your eating episodes?
No. Um... I don't take anything like that. Just... no.
Do you feel like you're eating much more quickly than usual during these episodes?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't paid attention to that. I guess I just... eat.
Do you think you're eating a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within a couple of hours?

Um... yeah. I guess so. It's... it's an amount that kind of scares me, honestly. That's sort of why I'm here. Like... at night, after I finish grading papers, I'll start with leftovers, but... then I just end up going through a bunch of other stuff. Cereal... crackers, peanut butter. Even, um... the snacks I pack for my classroom. So... yeah.
Do you usually eat these large amounts of food in response to stress, anxiety, or other emotions?
Um... I don't really know. I haven't really thought about it like that. I just... I don't really know why I do it.
Do you feel guilty after these episodes because of how much food you've eaten?
Um... I don't really know. I try not to think about it too much after it happens. I just kind of... clean up and go to sleep.
Do you ever eat large amounts of food without feeling like you're trying to make up for it afterwards?

Um... no, not really. I... I always feel like I have to fix it. Like, after one of those nights, I just... I'll tell myself I can't have breakfast or lunch the next day at school. And... I usually go out on the trail for a few hours, or force myself to do extra yoga. Even if I'm... you know, feeling really shaky and tired. I just... have to do it.
Do you feel like you're eating really fast during these episodes?
I guess so. I mean, I don't really time it or anything. It just... it happens.
Are you trying to keep from gaining weight when you restrict your food intake or exercise after one of these eating episodes?
Um... yeah, I guess so. I just... I don't want to put on weight. So I just do what I have to do. I don't really think about it much deeper than that.
Are you trying to prevent weight gain when you restrict food or exercise after these episodes?
Yeah... um, like I just said, I guess. I just... I really don't want to gain weight. That's... pretty much it.
Are you trying to burn off the calories you consumed during these eating episodes when you exercise afterwards?

Um... yeah. I mean, after one of those nights, I just... I tell myself I'm not allowed to eat breakfast or lunch at school the next day. And... yeah, I'll stay out on the trail for hours, or do extra yoga. Even when I'm feeling shaky and exhausted. I just... try to fix it, I guess.
Do you think that if you didn't exercise or restrict your food intake after these episodes, you would gain weight?
Um... yeah. I mean, if I didn't do all that, then... yeah, I'd probably gain weight. I don't really want to find out.
How often do you restrict your food intake or exercise after one of these eating episodes?

Um... well, it's pretty often, I guess. For the past few months, there hasn't really been a week where it doesn't happen at least once. I'll have a night where I just eat way too much, and then... the next day I have to skip meals at school or force myself to do a really long walk or extra yoga to make up for it. So... yeah, at least once a week.
Do you experience a significant amount of distress or guilt after these episodes of eating a large amount of food?
Um... yeah. I guess so. It's... not a great feeling. I just try not to think about it too much.

Do you experience a loss of control and eat an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most people would eat during a similar period of time and under similar circumstances during these episodes?

Um... yeah. I guess so. It's just... once I start, it's like I can't stop. It feels like the reasonable teacher part of me is just... watching from the outside, you know? Like she's saying, 'stop,' but... my hands just keep opening things. I just keep putting food in my mouth until I'm... painfully full. And it's definitely way more than a normal person would eat.
Do you experience these episodes of eating a large amount of food at least once a week for the past three months?

Um... yeah. Like I mentioned earlier... it's been at least once a week for the last few months. There really hasn't been a week without... one of those nights where I eat too much, and then have to skip my meals at school or do the extra yoga the next day to make up for it. So... yes.
